title: CockroachDB Stopped Publishing Its Source
caption:
I used to read CockroachDB's source when I wanted to understand how a real database works. That stops now.

On September 15 Cockroach Labs said new CockroachDB and Pebble releases will be developed in private repos. The public one stays up as a frozen snapshot and stops taking outside code. The license didn't change — the visibility did.

The reason is the part I keep chewing on. Not a competitor, not a fork. AI. They say models surface internals fast enough that publishing is now a security cost, and that they are already seeing AI used to produce functional reproductions of protected software. I don't have a good counterargument, and I don't like where it leads.

Would you close yours?

slides.headline:
The License
Didn’t Change
slides.sub: Same CockroachDB Software License, same pricing, same deployment. What changed is whether anyone outside can read the code.

slides.headline:
No More Outside
Contributions
slides.sub: Cockroach Labs will no longer accept code contributions to the core codebase. Bug and vulnerability reports still have a path.
